title: Over a Cohen–Macaulay local ring a finite module has a finite free resolution ending in a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of finite Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] with $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth] (that is, $\mathfrak m$ contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $d$; such an $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay). Let $M$ be a nonzero finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $e=\operatorname{depth}(M)$. Then $e\le d$, and there is an exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]

$$
0\to K\to F_{d-e-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to 0
$$

in which every $F_i$ is a finite free $R$-module ($F_i\cong R^{\oplus n_i}$ for some integer $n_i\ge0$) and $K$ is a finite $R$-module which is either $0$ or maximal Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(K)=d$. (When $e=d$ there are no $F_i$ and the sequence reads $0\to K\to M\to0$, i.e. $K\cong M$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NG (lemma-mcm-resolution, line 25411), with Lemma Tag 00NE (lemma-dimension-shift, line 25396), Definition Tag 00NF (definition-maximal-CM, line 25135) and, for $e\le d$, Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth, line 17814)

proof.text: ($0\le e\le d$.) $M$ is a nonzero finite module over the Noetherian local ring $R$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] (Stacks 00LK) $e=\operatorname{depth}(M)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$. Every chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of primes lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is a chain of prime ideals of $R$, so $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\le\dim R=d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Since $d$ is finite, $e$ is an integer with $0\le e\le d$ (in particular $e\neq\infty$, i.e. $\mathfrak mM\neq M$ in [def-weil-pbc-depth]). The same holds for every nonzero finite $R$-module, which is used in Steps 4-5.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth, lines 17813-17817); 'depth(M) <= dim(R)' is the remark after Definition Tag 00NF (definition-maximal-CM, lines 25134-25144)

Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NE (lemma-dimension-shift, lines 25398-25409): the term R^{\oplus n} there has depth d because R is Cohen-Macaulay; written out from Definition Tag 00LF (definition-regular-sequence) and Definition Tag 00LI (definition-depth)

proof.text: (Inductive claim and base.) For an integer $k$ with $0\le k\le d$ let $P(k)$ be the assertion: for every nonzero finite $R$-module $N$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $\operatorname{depth}(N)=d-k$ there are integers $n_0,\dots,n_{k-1}\ge1$ and an exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] $0\to K\to F_{k-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to N\to0$ with $F_i\cong R^{\oplus n_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and $K$ a nonzero finite $R$-module with $\operatorname{depth}(K)=d$ (for $k=0$ there are no $F_i$ and the sequence is $0\to K\to N\to0$). We prove $P(k)$ by induction on $k$. Base $k=0$: take $K=N$ and the identity $K\to N$; the sequence $0\to N\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}N\to0$ is exact, $K=N\neq0$ is finite and $\operatorname{depth}(K)=d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NG (lemma-mcm-resolution, lines 25410-25423): 'Immediate from the definition and Lemma 00NE'; the induction on d - e is the content of 'immediate', written out

proof.text:
(Inductive step: the first syzygy.) Let $1\le k\le d$, assume $P(k-1)$, and let $N
eq0$ be finite with $\operatorname{depth}(N)=e':=d-k<d$. Choose generators $x_1,\dots,x_n$ of $N$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; $n\ge1$ since $N
eq0$. The map $\pi:F_0=R^{\oplus n}	o N$, $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_ja_jx_j$, is surjective; let $K_1=\ker\pi$, so $0	o K_1	o F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}N	o0$ is a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. $F_0$ is a finite module over the Noetherian ring $R$, so its submodule $K_1$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. $K_1
eq0$: otherwise $\pi$ is an isomorphism $R^{\oplus n}\cong N$, and Step 2 gives $\operatorname{depth}(N)\ge d>e'$, a contradiction.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NE (lemma-dimension-shift, lines 25398-25409): the sequence 0 -> K -> R^{\oplus n} -> M -> 0; finiteness of K from Lemma Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic)

proof.text: (Depth of the syzygy: $\operatorname{depth}(K_1)=e'+1$.) In $0\to K_1\to F_0\to N\to0$ all three modules are nonzero and finite (Step 4), so [lem-weil-pbc-depth-in-ses] (Stacks 00LX) applies; $\operatorname{depth}(F_0)\ge d$ by Step 2 and $\operatorname{depth}(N)=e'$, $e'+1\le d$. By its part (3), $\operatorname{depth}(K_1)\ge\min\{\operatorname{depth}(F_0),e'+1\}\ge\min\{d,e'+1\}=e'+1$. By its part (2), $e'=\operatorname{depth}(N)\ge\min\{\operatorname{depth}(F_0),\operatorname{depth}(K_1)-1\}$; the minimum cannot be $\operatorname{depth}(F_0)\ge d>e'$, so it is $\operatorname{depth}(K_1)-1\le e'$. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(K_1)=e'+1=d-(k-1)$. (Stacks 00NE states only $\operatorname{depth}(K)>\operatorname{depth}(M)$; the equality, which the length $d-e$ of the resolution needs, uses part (2) of 00LX as well.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NE (lemma-dimension-shift, lines 25398-25409), whose proof is 'a special case of Lemma 00LX'; Lemma Tag 00LX (lemma-depth-in-ses, lines 17904-17916), parts (2) and (3)

proof.text: (Splicing.) By Steps 4-5, $K_1$ is a nonzero finite module of depth $d-(k-1)$, so $P(k-1)$ gives $0\to K\xrightarrow{\iota}G_{k-2}\to\cdots\to G_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}K_1\to0$ exact, $G_i\cong R^{\oplus m_i}$ with $m_i\ge1$, $K\neq0$ finite of depth $d$ (for $k=1$: $0\to K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}K_1\to0$, $\varepsilon$ an isomorphism). Put $F_i=G_{i-1}$ for $1\le i\le k-1$, with the maps of the $G$-sequence, and $F_1\to F_0$ the composite $G_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}K_1\hookrightarrow F_0$ (for $k=1$, $K\to F_0$ is $K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}K_1\hookrightarrow F_0$). The spliced sequence $0\to K\to F_{k-1}\to\cdots\to F_1\to F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}N\to0$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: at $N$, $\pi$ is onto; at $F_0$, the image of $F_1$ is $\varepsilon(G_0)=K_1=\ker\pi$; at $F_1=G_0$ (or at $K$ for $k=1$), the kernel of $G_0\to F_0$ equals $\ker\varepsilon$ because $K_1\hookrightarrow F_0$ is injective, and $\ker\varepsilon$ is the image of $G_1$ (of $0$, resp. $K\to K_1$ is injective, for $k=1$); at the other places exactness is that of the $G$-sequence. So $P(k)$ holds for $N$, which completes the induction.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NG (lemma-mcm-resolution, lines 25410-25423): 'Immediate from the definition and Lemma 00NE'; splicing written out

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By Step 1, $e=\operatorname{depth}(M)$ is an integer with $0\le e\le d$; with $k=d-e$, $P(d-e)$ (Steps 3-6) gives an exact sequence $0\to K\to F_{d-e-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to0$ with every $F_i\cong R^{\oplus n_i}$ finite free and $K$ a finite $R$-module with $\operatorname{depth}(K)=d$, i.e. maximal Cohen-Macaulay (Stacks 00NF); in particular $K$ is $0$ or of depth $d$, as stated (the proof shows $K\neq0$). For $e=d$ the sequence is $0\to K\to M\to0$, $K=M$.

split_report.summary: Read 00NG, 00NE, 00LX, 00LK and 00NF in algebra.tex (tags verified in tags/tags). Statement kept; stmt_deps gains def-weil-pbc-free-module (F_i finite free). Proof in seven steps: e <= d from 00LK (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension) and dim Supp(M) <= dim R; free modules R^n (n >= 1) have depth >= d (written out from the definitions); induction on k = d - e with the explicit claim P(k) (nonzero finite N of depth d - k has 0 -> K -> F_{k-1} -> ... -> F_0 -> N -> 0, F_i finite free, K nonzero finite of depth d), base K = N; inductive step: surjection R^n -> N, kernel K_1 finite (existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite) and nonzero (else N free of depth >= d), depth K_1 = e' + 1 from 00LX (2) and (3) (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-depth-in-ses; 00NE alone gives only depth K_1 > e', which does not give the exact length d - e), then splicing. No 00NE node is created: it is the special case of 00LX the step uses directly. The proof gives K != 0, so the 'K = 0' alternative of the statement never occurs for M != 0 (the source gap recorded for 00NG is closed). Mathlib (pinned) has no depth: both new nodes unsplit with mathlib_candidate (KrullDimension/Regular.lean:197, Depth/Rees.lean:158).
